newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page - Feb 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page - Feb 27.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Feb. 27:

WASHINGTON - In a major shake-up of the D.C. police department, Chief Larry Soulsby unveiled a crime plan that includes redeploying 400 officers who will concentrate on reducing homicides, gangs and open-air drug markets.

WASHINGTON - Freshman Democratic Senator Robert Torricelli announced he will oppose the balanced budget amendment to the Constitution, virtually assuring its defeat and foiling a top priority of Republican leaders.
WASHINGTON - Key Senate Republicans want to exclude Congressional campaign practices from a planned probe into election fund-raising abuses and put the focus on the 1996 presidential race.
JERUSALEM - Israel pressed ahead with plans to build a new neighborhood for 30,000 Jews in East Jerusalem, the largest Jewish residential project since 1980 in the holy city's disputed Arab portion.
RICHMOND - Virginia officials say they will not enforce new federal regulations taking effect Friday that require tobacco buyers younger than 27 to produce photo identification.
WASHINGTON - An astonishing discovery of 400,000-year-old spears in the depths of a German coal mine may drastically rewrite the history of early Stone Age humans in Europe.
